topic: Variadic Templates for Flexible Argument Handling
explanation: Variadic templates in C++ allow functions to accept a variable number of arguments of different types, enabling flexible and reusable code. This is particularly useful in real-world scenarios like logging, error reporting, or processing collections of data. Best practices include using recursion to handle the argument pack, ensuring a base case to prevent infinite recursion, and maintaining idiomatic C++ by leveraging type safety and avoiding unnecessary copies with const references. Common pitfalls include forgetting the base case, which can lead to compiler errors, or overusing variadic functions when simpler alternatives suffice; to avoid this, always profile for performance and readability.
